@graph.name: Plate Reader Endpoint Assay Workflow
@graph.description: A metadata-driven R workflow for processing endpoint colorimetric and fluorescence assays from 96-well microplate readers. Parses raw instrument exports (SpectraMax iD3 or BioTek Synergy 2) or a user-prepared .xlsx file for any other instrument, subtracts blanks, fits a linear standard curve, back-calculates sample concentrations (flagging out-of-range samples as extrapolated rather than dropping them), and exports plate-map, standard-curve, and sample-value plots and CSVs.

@graph.name: SpectraMax endpoint assay pipeline
@graph.description: Parses SpectraMax iD3 SDA endpoint-assay exports (.csv, .xls, or .txt), auto-detecting absorbance vs. fluorescence read mode and the measured wavelength(s). Subtracts blank signal, evaluates the assay's signal formula, fits a linear standard curve, and back-calculates sample concentrations. See examples/example_run/ (BCA, absorbance) and examples/example_run_amplexred/ (Amplex Red H2O2, fluorescence) for runnable demonstrations.

@graph.name: BioTek Synergy 2 endpoint assay pipeline
@graph.description: The same pipeline as process_spectramax_endpoint_std_curve.R, adapted for BioTek Synergy 2 Gen5 .xlsx exports. Only raw-file parsing differs between the two scripts; blank correction, signal formula, standard curve, plotting, and outputs are identical.

@graph.name: Generic Excel endpoint assay pipeline
@graph.description: The same pipeline as process_spectramax_endpoint_std_curve.R, but reads a user-prepared .xlsx file instead of an instrument-specific export, for use with any plate reader. Auto-detects a long format (single sheet, columns well/wavelength/signal) or a plate format (one 8x12-grid sheet per wavelength, sheet name = wavelength) from the first sheet's cell A1. Only raw-file parsing differs from the other two scripts; blank correction, signal formula, standard curve, plotting, and outputs are identical.

@graph.name: Generic Excel input example run (both formats)
@graph.description: Runs process_generic_excel_endpoint_std_curve.R against the same fabricated two-wavelength (A412 - A700) assay data encoded twice: once as a long-format .xlsx and once as a plate-format .xlsx. Asserts both back-calculate to the same sample concentrations, demonstrating the two input formats are equivalent.
